title: Ulyana and the Garden
premise: Yara Reyes has spent his life keeping the last smugglers' guild of Thornfell alive by staying small, unseen, and indispensable—until prayers he never meant to offer start being answered by gods everyone believed dead. The old gods, waking hungry after a century of silence, mistake Yara for the heir of the bloodline that once bound them, and the guild's dying matriarch confirms it: he is the last of the Wardens, the family that sealed the gods away and then erased themselves from history. To survive, Yara must find the Warden door out of a country that officially no longer exists, guided by Ulyana, a disgraced priestess of the garden faith who once tried to kill him. As imperial hunters, rival smugglers, and the gods themselves close in, Yara learns that the door out is also the door that keeps the old gods caged, and opening it for himself means opening it for them. In the end Yara chooses to stay, taking up the Warden burden willingly—but he does not carry it alone, because Ulyana chooses exile from her faith to stand beside him, and together they become the garden's new keepers.
about_author: Zephyrine Nakamura is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. Their work blends folklore, border politics, and quiet acts of defiance, and 'Ulyana and the Garden' is their first novel.

chapters.title: Salt Roads
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara guides a salt caravan through the Thornfell passes while dodging imperial tollmen, establishing his gift for invisibility and his loyalty to the guild's aging matriarch, Baba Sef. When a stranger's desperate prayer at a roadside shrine is audibly answered, Yara feels the mountain shudder. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Guild of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara returns to the guildhall, a crumbling waystation of thirteen smugglers, and delivers his cut to Baba Sef, who is visibly failing. She asks him strange questions about his grandmother's name and the old Warden seal. He deflects. Beat: the comfort of found family fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: What the Shrine Gave Back
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana, a garden-priestess stripped of her order for heresy, tends a neglected shrine and witnesses a god take root in the soil—hungry, half-remembered, and asking for 'the Warden's blood.' She recognizes the name from her order's forbidden archives. Beat: dread and forbidden wonder.

chapters.title: The Prayer He Didn't Mean
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Trapped in a rockslide, Yara curses the old gods by name—names he shouldn't know—and the mountain moves for him. He escapes unharmed but marked, a green sigil burned into his palm. Beat: terror at discovering he is not ordinary.

chapters.title: Baba Sef's Confession
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Baba Sef reveals the guild was founded as a Warden hiding place, and Yara's grandmother was the last Warden of Thornfell. She gives him a rusted key and a warning: the gods waking means the seal is failing. Beat: inheritance as a wound.

chapters.title: The Priestess with a Knife
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana is sent by her former order to find and kill the Warden heir before the gods can use him. She traces the sigil's echo to the guildhall and finds Yara mending nets. She hesitates one heartbeat too long. Beat: duty colliding with recognition.

chapters.title: Thirteen Against the Empire
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Imperial inquisitors raid the guildhall hunting the 'anomalous prayer-signature.' The smugglers scatter; Baba Sef is captured buying Yara time. Yara flees with the key and nothing else. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Liars
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara corners Ulyana in a border town, disarms her, and instead of killing her proposes the unthinkable: she knows the old rites, he knows the roads—together they can find the Warden door. She agrees for her own reasons. Beat: wary, electric trust.

chapters.title: The Garden That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana leads Yara through a hidden valley where the garden faith once flourished; the waking god there offers Yara power in exchange for opening 'the door.' He refuses, and the god marks him as prey. Beat: temptation and refusal.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Ghost
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In a dead surveyor's archive, they find maps of a country that no longer exists—old Thornfell, before the empire redrew it. The Warden door lies at the heart of the erased borders. Beat: hope sharpened by the map's impossibility.

chapters.title: What Ulyana Buried
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana confesses her heresy: she once opened a minor shrine-gate and let something through, killing three pilgrims, which is why her order exiled her—and why she was chosen to kill the Warden. Yara chooses to trust her anyway. Beat: confession as turning point.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A river god demands a toll of true names to let them cross its flooded gorge. Yara gives his Warden name freely, and the god, moved, warns them: another hunts the door, wearing a familiar face. Beat: the cost of honesty.

chapters.title: The Face at the Fire
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Baba Sef appears at their campfire, freed—or so it seems. Yara realizes too late it is a god wearing her shape, probing him for the door's location. Ulyana's rites drive it off, but it has learned enough. Beat: violation of the one safe memory.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Imperial inquisitor Dame Corvane catches them but, hearing Ulyana's account of the waking gods, reveals the empire has known for a year—and plans to burn the mountains and everyone in them. She lets them go with a map fragment. Beat: enemies realigned by larger fear.

chapters.title: The Guild Reassembles
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara finds the scattered smugglers and, for the first time, leads rather than hides. They agree to hold the pass against the imperial burn-teams while he reaches the door. Beat: invisibility surrendered for leadership.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Dead Country
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the heart of the erased borders, Yara finds the Warden door: not an exit but a lock, and his blood is the key. Opening it for himself would free every caged god. He finally understands what his grandmother died to keep shut. Beat: the premise's terrible truth.

chapters.title: Ulyana's Choice
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana's order arrives to complete the killing she refused, offering her reinstatement if she opens the door as sacrifice. She burns her priestess vows instead and takes up Yara's side of the Warden rite. Beat: love chosen over duty.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Garden
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Gods, inquisitors, and the guild converge on the door as the seal cracks. Baba Sef, genuinely freed, dies holding the pass so Yara can complete the rite. Beat: sacrifice stacking toward the climax.

chapters.title: The Warden's Blood
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the door, the eldest god offers Yara everything—his guild restored, his country un-erased—if he opens it. Yara refuses and, with Ulyana, reseals the door using not a bloodline but a freely given vow. Beat: the climax; power refused.

chapters.title: After the Sealing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The mountains quiet; the empire's burn order is quietly shelved when the 'anomaly' vanishes. Ulyana and Yara bury Baba Sef at the garden shrine, and the smugglers begin rebuilding the guild around them. Beat: exhausted, tender aftermath.

chapters.title: The Gardeners
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara and Ulyana take up residence as the door's keepers, tending the shrine-valley where the garden faith is quietly reborn—not caging the old gods now, but teaching them to be worshipped rather than feared. Beat: transformation of duty into vocation.

chapters.title: A Country That Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, coda. Years later, travelers speak of a green valley in the Thornfells where prayers are answered kindly, and a smuggler's road that always finds you home. Yara, no longer invisible but finally at peace, opens the gate for the next lost soul. Beat: resolution and quiet hope.
